meta.title: Eyes on the chips: the seaside war between humans and gulls
meta.deck: Across the world's beach towns, bold seabirds have learned that tourists are an easy meal. Scientists think they have found a surprisingly simple defence.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: Eyes on the chips: the seaside war between humans and gulls
sents.zh: 盯紧你的薯条：海边的人鸥大战
notes: Eyes on the chips：省略了动词的祈使说法，相当于 Keep your eyes on the chips，“盯紧薯条”。
chips 在英式英语里是炸薯条（美式叫 fries），fish and chips 就是炸鱼薯条。
seaside：海边的、海滨的，常指度假的海滨小镇。

sents.en: Across the world's beach towns, bold seabirds have learned that tourists are an easy meal.
sents.zh: 在世界各地的海滩小镇，胆大的海鸟已经摸清了：游客就是送上门的一顿饭。
notes: bold：大胆的、放肆的，这里说海鸟一点不怕人。
an easy meal：轻松到手的一顿饭，把游客比作猎物，有点幽默。
have learned 用现在完成时，说明这是它们已经学会的本事。

sents.en: Scientists think they have found a surprisingly simple defence.
sents.zh: 科学家认为，他们找到了一个简单得出奇的防御办法。
notes: surprisingly simple：副词修饰形容词，“简单得出人意料”。
defence：防御、防守，英式拼写；美式拼作 defense。

sents.en: It happens in a flash.
sents.zh: 事情就发生在一眨眼之间。
notes: in a flash：一瞬间、转眼之间。flash 是闪光，像闪光一样快。
开头一个短句，先制造悬念。

sents.en: A family sits down on a sea wall in Cornwall, unwraps a paper parcel of fish and chips, and before anyone has taken a bite, a herring gull swoops down and makes off with the biggest piece.
sents.zh: 一家人在康沃尔的海堤上坐下，拆开一包用纸裹着的炸鱼薯条，还没等谁咬上一口，一只银鸥就俯冲下来，叼走了最大的那块。
notes: 句子用一般现在时讲故事，像现场直播，读起来更生动。
unwrap：拆开（包装）。un- 表示相反，wrap 是包。
swoop down：猛地俯冲下来，多用于鸟。
make off with：拿了……就跑、偷走。

sents.en: The children shriek, the parents shout, and the bird retreats to a rooftop to enjoy its prize.
sents.zh: 孩子们尖叫，大人们大喊，那只鸟则退到屋顶上享用它的战利品。
notes: 三个短句并列，节奏很快，像镜头一个接一个切换。
shriek：尖叫，声音又高又刺耳。
retreat：撤退、退回到安全的地方。
prize：奖品，这里幽默地指抢到的薯条。

sents.en: Similar scenes play out every summer from Brighton to Sydney to Cape Town.
sents.zh: 从布莱顿到悉尼再到开普敦，每年夏天都在上演类似的场面。
notes: play out：（事情）发生、上演，像戏一样演出来。
from A to B to C：列举范围很广的地方，说明到处都这样。

sents.en: Gulls were not always this cheeky.
sents.zh: 海鸥并不是一直都这么厚脸皮。
notes: this + 形容词：这么……。this cheeky = 这么放肆。
cheeky：厚脸皮的、没大没小的，英式口语，常带一点好笑的意味。

sents.en: For most of their history they fed at sea, scavenging behind fishing boats and picking through the shoreline.
sents.zh: 在漫长的历史中，它们大多在海上觅食，跟在渔船后面捡食，在海岸边翻找吃的。
notes: fed 是 feed 的过去式，这里是不及物用法“进食、觅食”。
scavenge：（动物）找腐食、捡剩下的吃；（人）在垃圾里翻找东西。
pick through：在一堆东西里仔细翻找。
两个 -ing 短语作伴随状语，说明它们怎么觅食。

sents.en: But as fish stocks dwindled and towns filled up with litter, rubbish bins and outdoor diners, many birds moved inland and adapted with remarkable speed.
sents.zh: 可随着鱼类资源越来越少，镇上到处是垃圾、垃圾桶和露天吃饭的人，许多海鸥搬到了内陆，而且适应得快得惊人。
notes: as 引导时间兼原因状语：随着……。
fish stocks：鱼类资源、鱼群数量。dwindle：逐渐减少。
fill up with：被……填满。
inland：在内陆、往内陆。adapt：适应。

sents.en: A city gull can live for 20 years, remembers where food is easy to come by, and learns by watching other gulls get away with theft.
sents.zh: 一只城市海鸥能活二十年，记得哪里容易找到吃的，还会看着别的海鸥偷了东西没事，跟着学。
notes: 三个谓语并列：can live, remembers, learns。
easy to come by：容易弄到。come by = 得到、弄到。
watch + 宾语 + 动词原形：看着某事发生。get away with sth：做了坏事却没受惩罚。

sents.en: Residents are at their wits' end.
sents.zh: 居民们已经无计可施了。
notes: at one's wits' end：束手无策、急得不知怎么办才好。wits 指头脑、智力，wits' end 就是“脑子用到头了”。

sents.en: Councils have tried everything from spiked roofs and fake owls to fines for anyone caught feeding the birds.
sents.zh: 地方政府什么办法都试过：从在屋顶装尖刺、摆假猫头鹰，到对被抓到喂鸟的人罚款。
notes: council：地方议会、地方政府，英式用法。
everything from A to B：从 A 到 B 什么都……，用来说范围广。
fine 作名词：罚款。caught feeding the birds = 被抓到在喂鸟。

sents.en: Some towns have hired falconers, whose hawks patrol the beach to scare gulls off.
sents.zh: 有些镇雇了驯鹰人，让他们的鹰在海滩上巡逻，把海鸥吓跑。
notes: falconer：驯鹰人。whose 引导定语从句，“驯鹰人的鹰”。
patrol：巡逻。
scare sb off：把……吓跑。宾语可以放中间：scare gulls off。

sents.en: Most of these measures work for a while; then the gulls catch on and come back.
sents.zh: 这些办法大多能管用一阵子，然后海鸥就看穿了，又回来了。
notes: measures：措施、办法，常用复数。
for a while：一段时间。
catch on：明白过来、领会。另一个意思是“流行起来”：The idea caught on.。

sents.en: Researchers studying gull behaviour have come up with a cheaper idea: stare them down.
sents.zh: 研究海鸥行为的研究人员想出了一个更省钱的办法：瞪着它们，直到它们退缩。
notes: studying gull behaviour 是现在分词短语，修饰 researchers。behaviour 是英式拼写。
come up with：想出（主意、办法）。
stare sb down：盯着对方直到对方退缩。

sents.en: In one experiment, scientists placed a bag of chips on the ground and watched how long passing gulls took to approach it.
sents.zh: 在一项实验里，科学家把一袋薯条放在地上，观察路过的海鸥要过多久才会靠近。
notes: how long passing gulls took to approach it 是宾语从句，用陈述语序。
passing：路过的，现在分词作定语。
approach：靠近、接近，及物动词，后面直接跟宾语，不加 to。

sents.en: When a person kept their eyes fixed on the bird, it hesitated far longer than when the person looked away, and many gave up altogether.
sents.zh: 如果人一直盯着鸟看，它犹豫的时间比人把目光移开时长得多，很多干脆放弃了。
notes: keep one's eyes fixed on：目光一直盯着。
hesitate：犹豫。far longer：far 加强比较级，“长得多”。
give up：放弃。altogether：完全、彻底。

sents.en: Gulls, it seems, are wary of being watched, perhaps because a staring animal is more likely to fight back.
sents.zh: 看来，海鸥不喜欢被人盯着，也许是因为一个瞪着你的动物更可能会反击。
notes: it seems 是插入语，“看起来”。
be wary of：对……有戒心、提防。wary of being watched = 提防被人盯着。
fight back：还击、反抗。

sents.en: There is a catch, of course.
sents.zh: 当然，这里面也有个问题。
notes: There is a catch：有个隐藏的问题、有个“但是”。catch 作名词是“暗藏的问题、圈套”。
这是一个转折句，引出下面的局限。

sents.en: Only a minority of the gulls dared to come near the food, and the boldest barely paused before grabbing it.
sents.zh: 只有少数海鸥敢靠近食物，而胆子最大的那几只几乎不停顿就抢走了。
notes: a minority of：……中的少数。反义是 the majority of（大多数）。
dare to do sth：敢于做某事。
barely：几乎没有、勉强。barely paused = 几乎没停。

sents.en: And it is hard to keep an eye on a gull while also eating, chatting and keeping track of small children.
sents.zh: 而且一边吃东西、聊天、看着小孩，一边还要盯住一只海鸥，实在不容易。
notes: it is hard to ... 是形式主语句，真正的主语是不定式。
keep an eye on：看着、留意。
keep track of：随时掌握……的情况、不让……跑丢。

sents.en: Still, the finding hints at something that frustrated towns often miss.
sents.zh: 不过，这个发现指出了一点，焦头烂额的小镇常常忽略。
notes: the finding：研究发现，可数名词。
hint at：暗示、透露出。
frustrated：恼火的、沮丧的，这里形容那些拿海鸥没办法的小镇。

sents.en: Gulls are not villains; they are opportunists doing what any sensible animal would do when food is left lying around.
sents.zh: 海鸥并不是坏蛋；它们只是投机者，吃的东西随便放着的时候，任何聪明的动物都会这么做。
notes: villain：（故事里的）坏人、反派。
opportunist：投机者、会抓机会的人（或动物），这里不算贬义。
leave sth lying around：把东西随手乱放。

sents.en: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.
sents.zh: 许多种类的海鸥在海上数量正在减少，而它们城里的“亲戚”却过得很好，所以很难找到理由去捕杀它们。
notes: in decline：在衰退、数量在减少。
even as：正当……的时候（表示对比）。
thrive：茁壮成长、兴旺。urban cousins：城里的同类，cousins 是比喻。
which 指前面整件事。cull：（为控制数量）捕杀；hard to justify：很难说得过去。

sents.en: The best defence may simply be to eat indoors, keep bins closed and, when all else fails, look the bird in the eye.
sents.zh: 最好的防御办法也许就是：在室内吃饭，盖好垃圾桶，实在不行，就直视那只鸟的眼睛。
notes: to eat ... keep ... look ... 三个不定式并列作表语。
when all else fails：当其他办法都不管用时。
look sb in the eye：直视某人的眼睛，常表示坦然或对抗。

sents.en: It will not win the war, but it might save your lunch.
sents.zh: 这赢不了整场战争，但也许能保住你的午饭。
notes: the war 呼应标题里的 war，首尾呼应。
结尾一句举重若轻：大问题解决不了，小事还能顾上，带点幽默。

vocab.note: seaside 常作定语：a seaside town（海滨小镇）、a seaside holiday（海边度假）。go to the seaside = 去海边玩，英式说法。

ex.en: We spent a week in a small [[seaside]] town.
ex.zh: 我们在一个海边小镇住了一周。

ex.en: Every August the family goes to the [[seaside]].
ex.zh: 每年八月，一家人都去海边。

vocab.note: bold 可褒可贬：a bold plan（大胆的计划）；说动物或孩子 bold，常带“胆子大到不客气”的意思。比较级 bolder，最高级 boldest。

ex.en: The [[bold]] squirrel took a nut right out of my hand.
ex.zh: 那只胆大的松鼠直接从我手里拿走了坚果。

ex.en: It was a [[bold]] decision to quit her job.
ex.zh: 辞掉工作是个大胆的决定。

vocab.note: 英式 defence，美式 defense。a defence against sth = 抵御……的办法。动词是 defend。

ex.en: Sunscreen is your best [[defence]] against sunburn.
ex.zh: 防晒霜是防晒伤最好的办法。

ex.en: The castle walls were the town's main [[defence]].
ex.zh: 城墙是这座城镇主要的防御。

vocab.note: 同义说法：in an instant、in no time。I'll be back in a flash. = 我马上回来。

ex.en: The cake was gone [[in a flash]].
ex.zh: 蛋糕一眨眼就没了。

ex.en: I'll be back [[in a flash]].
ex.zh: 我马上回来。

vocab.note: un- 表示相反的动作：wrap（包）→ unwrap（拆开）；lock → unlock；pack → unpack。

ex.en: The kids [[unwrapped]] their presents in seconds.
ex.zh: 孩子们几秒钟就把礼物拆开了。

ex.en: She [[unwraps]] a sandwich at her desk every day at noon.
ex.zh: 她每天中午在办公桌前拆开一个三明治。

vocab.note: swoop 指鸟从空中猛扑下来，也可以比喻突然行动：Police swooped on the house.（警察突袭了那栋房子。）

ex.en: An owl [[swooped down]] and caught a mouse.
ex.zh: 一只猫头鹰俯冲下来抓住了一只老鼠。

ex.en: Watch the eagle [[swoop down]] towards the river.
ex.zh: 看那只鹰朝河面俯冲下去。

vocab.note: make off = 匆匆逃走；make off with sth = 带着（偷来的）东西跑掉。比 steal 更口语，更有画面感。

ex.en: A thief [[made off with]] her handbag.
ex.zh: 一个小偷抢了她的手提包就跑了。

ex.en: The dog [[made off with]] a sausage from the barbecue.
ex.zh: 狗从烧烤架上叼了一根香肠就跑。

vocab.note: shriek 比 scream 更尖、更短。shriek with laughter = 笑得尖叫。也可作名词：a shriek of delight。

ex.en: The kids [[shrieked]] when the cold wave hit them.
ex.zh: 冰冷的浪打过来，孩子们尖叫起来。

ex.en: She [[shrieked]] with laughter at the joke.
ex.zh: 她听到笑话笑得尖叫。

vocab.note: retreat 原是军事用语“撤退”，也常用于日常：retreat to one's room（躲回自己房间）。名词 a retreat 还可以指静修的地方。

ex.en: The cat [[retreated]] under the bed when the guests arrived.
ex.zh: 客人一来，猫就躲到床底下去了。

ex.en: After lunch he [[retreats]] to his study to read.
ex.zh: 午饭后他总是躲进书房看书。

vocab.note: play out 指事情一步步展开、发生，常用于场景、局面：We'll see how things play out.（看事情怎么发展吧。）

ex.en: The same argument [[plays out]] in our house every Sunday.
ex.zh: 每个星期天，我们家都会上演同样的争吵。

ex.en: Let's wait and see how things [[play out]].
ex.zh: 我们等着看事情怎么发展吧。

vocab.note: 英式口语，常说小孩或宠物，不算很重的批评，带一点好笑：a cheeky grin（调皮的笑）。

ex.en: Don't be [[cheeky]] to your teacher.
ex.zh: 别对老师没大没小的。

ex.en: He gave me a [[cheeky]] grin and took the last biscuit.
ex.zh: 他冲我调皮一笑，拿走了最后一块饼干。

vocab.note: scavenger 指食腐动物，比如秃鹫、鬣狗。人也可以 scavenge for sth：在旧物里翻找能用的东西。

ex.en: Foxes [[scavenge]] for scraps in the bins at night.
ex.zh: 狐狸夜里在垃圾桶里翻找残羹剩饭。

ex.en: We [[scavenged]] wood from the beach for the fire.
ex.zh: 我们在海滩上捡木头生火。

vocab.note: pick through 强调一件件地挑、翻：pick through the rubbish / the evidence。

ex.en: She [[picked through]] the box of old photos.
ex.zh: 她把那箱旧照片翻了个遍。

ex.en: Birds were [[picking through]] the rubbish.
ex.zh: 几只鸟在垃圾里翻找。

vocab.note: dwindle 强调慢慢变少、越来越小：dwindling numbers（越来越少的数量）。近义 shrink，但 dwindle 更强调“所剩无几”。

ex.en: Our savings [[dwindled]] during the long holiday.
ex.zh: 长假期间我们的积蓄越来越少。

ex.en: The crowd [[dwindled]] as the rain got heavier.
ex.zh: 雨越下越大，人群渐渐散去。

vocab.note: fill up 是装满；fill up with sth 说明用什么装满。也说加满油：fill up the car。

ex.en: The room soon [[filled up with]] smoke.
ex.zh: 房间里很快烟雾弥漫。

ex.en: Her eyes [[filled up with]] tears.
ex.zh: 她的眼里噙满了泪水。

vocab.note: inland 可作副词（move inland）也可作形容词（an inland city，内陆城市）。反义是 coastal（沿海的）。

ex.en: The storm moved [[inland]] overnight.
ex.zh: 风暴一夜之间移到了内陆。

ex.en: They live in a small [[inland]] village.
ex.zh: 他们住在一个内陆小村子里。

vocab.note: adapt to sth：适应……。adapt 也可以表示“改编”：adapt a novel for the screen。形容词 adaptable = 适应力强的。

ex.en: Children [[adapt]] quickly to a new school.
ex.zh: 孩子们很快就能适应新学校。

ex.en: The company [[adapted]] to online sales.
ex.zh: 公司转向了网上销售。

vocab.note: come by sth = 得到、弄到。常用 hard to come by（难得、不好找）：Good jobs are hard to come by.

ex.en: Cheap flats are hard to [[come by]] in London.
ex.zh: 在伦敦很难找到便宜的公寓。

ex.en: In summer, fresh fruit is [[easy to come by]].
ex.zh: 夏天新鲜水果很容易买到。

vocab.note: get away with sth：做了错事却逃过惩罚。You won't get away with this! = 你逃不掉的！

ex.en: He cheated and [[got away with]] it.
ex.zh: 他作弊了，却什么事也没有。

ex.en: You can't [[get away with]] being late every day.
ex.zh: 你不能天天迟到还不受处罚。

vocab.note: 注意 wits' 的撇号在 s 后面（复数所有格）。常说 I'm at my wits' end. = 我真是没辙了。

ex.en: The new parents were [[at their wits' end]] after a week without sleep.
ex.zh: 一周没睡好，这对新手父母已经束手无策了。

ex.en: I'm [[at my wits' end]] with this printer.
ex.zh: 这台打印机真让我没辙了。

vocab.zh: 从 A 到 B 什么都……
vocab.note: 用来表示种类繁多：The shop sells everything from socks to sofas.

ex.en: The market sells [[everything from]] fish to phone cases.
ex.zh: 这个市场什么都卖，从鱼到手机壳。

ex.en: We talked about [[everything from]] football to philosophy.
ex.zh: 我们什么都聊，从足球到哲学。

vocab.note: fine 作名词是“罚款”，作动词是“处以罚款”：He was fined £100. 别和形容词 fine（好的）弄混。

ex.en: She got a parking [[fine]] outside the hospital.
ex.zh: 她在医院外面吃了一张停车罚单。

ex.en: Drivers are [[fined]] for using their phones.
ex.zh: 司机开车用手机会被罚款。

vocab.note: scare sb/sth off 或 scare off sb/sth。也说 scare away。比喻用法：High prices scared buyers off.（高价把买家吓跑了。）

ex.en: The dog barked and [[scared]] the burglars off.
ex.zh: 狗一叫，把小偷吓跑了。

ex.en: High prices may [[scare off]] tourists.
ex.zh: 高价可能会把游客吓跑。

vocab.note: 两个常用意思：一是“领会、反应过来”（The kids caught on fast.）；二是“流行起来”（The fashion never caught on.）。

ex.en: It took me a while to [[catch on]] to the joke.
ex.zh: 我过了一会儿才明白这个笑话。

ex.en: The new app never really [[caught on]].
ex.zh: 这个新应用一直没真正流行起来。

vocab.note: come up with an idea / a plan / an answer / an excuse。比 think of 更强调“想出来了”。

ex.en: She [[came up with]] a clever name for the shop.
ex.zh: 她给店想了个巧妙的名字。

ex.en: We need to [[come up with]] a plan by Friday.
ex.zh: 我们得在周五前想出个计划。

vocab.note: stare at sb = 盯着某人看；stare sb down 更进一步，盯到对方先移开目光或退缩。

ex.en: The cat [[stared]] the dog down.
ex.zh: 猫一直瞪着狗，直到狗退缩。

ex.en: Don't try to [[stare down]] an angry bull.
ex.zh: 别跟一头发怒的公牛对视。

vocab.note: approach 作动词时直接跟宾语：approach the door（不说 approach to）。也可以指“着手处理”：approach a problem。

ex.en: A stranger [[approached]] me in the street.
ex.zh: 街上有个陌生人朝我走过来。

ex.en: Winter is [[approaching]] fast.
ex.zh: 冬天很快就要到了。

vocab.note: hesitate to do sth：迟疑着不做。礼貌用语 Don't hesitate to ask. = 有问题尽管问。名词 hesitation。

ex.en: She [[hesitated]] before opening the letter.
ex.zh: 她犹豫了一下才拆开信。

ex.en: Don't [[hesitate]] to call me if you need help.
ex.zh: 需要帮忙就尽管给我打电话。

vocab.note: give up (doing) sth：放弃、戒掉：give up smoking。give up on sb = 对某人不抱希望。

ex.en: He [[gave up]] after three tries.
ex.zh: 他试了三次就放弃了。

ex.en: Never [[give up]] on your dreams.
ex.zh: 永远不要放弃你的梦想。

vocab.note: altogether 有两个意思：一是“完全”（stop altogether），二是“总共”（£50 altogether）。注意和 all together（大家一起）区分。

ex.en: The noise stopped [[altogether]].
ex.zh: 噪音完全停了。

ex.en: We might cancel the trip [[altogether]].
ex.zh: 我们可能会彻底取消这次旅行。

vocab.note: wary 指小心提防，比 careful 多一层“不信任”：be wary of strangers。名词形式 wariness。

ex.en: Cats are [[wary of]] strangers.
ex.zh: 猫对陌生人有戒心。

ex.en: Be [[wary of]] offers that sound too good to be true.
ex.zh: 好得不像真的优惠，要多留个心眼。

vocab.note: fight back 也可以指“忍住（眼泪等）”：fight back tears。

ex.en: When the bully pushed him, he [[fought back]].
ex.zh: 那个恶霸推他时，他还手了。

ex.en: She [[fought back]] tears during the speech.
ex.zh: 她演讲时强忍着眼泪。

vocab.zh: 有个隐藏的问题、有个“但是”
vocab.note: catch 作名词指暗藏的问题或代价。常见问法：What's the catch?（有什么猫腻？）

ex.en: The flight is very cheap, but [[there is a catch]]: no luggage.
ex.zh: 机票很便宜，但有个问题：不含行李。

ex.en: Free pizza for a year? [[What's the catch]]?
ex.zh: 一年免费披萨？有什么猫腻？

vocab.note: 反义 the majority of（大多数）。in the minority = 属于少数。

ex.en: Only [[a minority of]] students walk to school.
ex.zh: 只有少数学生走路上学。

ex.en: [[A minority of]] drivers cause most accidents.
ex.zh: 大多数事故是少数司机造成的。

vocab.note: dare 可以接 to do 或直接接动词原形：He didn't dare (to) look.。I dare you to ... = 我赌你不敢……。

ex.en: Nobody [[dared to]] tell the boss.
ex.zh: 没人敢告诉老板。

ex.en: I didn't [[dare]] look down from the bridge.
ex.zh: 我不敢从桥上往下看。

vocab.note: barely 带否定意味：I barely slept. = 我几乎没睡。也表示“刚刚够”：She barely caught the train.（她差点没赶上火车。）

ex.en: I could [[barely]] hear him over the music.
ex.zh: 音乐太吵，我几乎听不见他说话。

ex.en: We [[barely]] made it to the airport on time.
ex.zh: 我们差一点就没按时赶到机场。

vocab.note: keep an eye on sb/sth：照看、留心。Can you keep an eye on my bag? = 能帮我看一下包吗？

ex.en: Can you [[keep an eye on]] my bag for a minute?
ex.zh: 能帮我看一下包吗？

ex.en: The teacher [[kept an eye on]] the quiet boy at the back.
ex.zh: 老师一直留意着后排那个安静的男孩。

vocab.note: keep track of sth：随时了解、记录。反义 lose track of：搞不清、忘了。lose track of time = 忘了时间。

ex.en: I use an app to [[keep track of]] my spending.
ex.zh: 我用一个应用记录开支。

ex.en: We [[lost track of]] time and missed the bus.
ex.zh: 我们忘了时间，错过了公交车。

vocab.note: hint 作名词是“暗示、提示”：give sb a hint。hint at sth = 间接地提到、暗示。

ex.en: He [[hinted at]] a big announcement next week.
ex.zh: 他暗示下周会有重大消息。

ex.en: The dark clouds [[hint at]] a storm.
ex.zh: 乌云预示着暴风雨。

vocab.zh: 投机者、善于抓机会的人
vocab.note: opportunist 常带贬义，指只顾自己利益抓机会的人；说动物时就是“见机行事”。形容词 opportunistic。

ex.en: Foxes are clever [[opportunists]] that eat almost anything.
ex.zh: 狐狸是聪明的机会主义者，几乎什么都吃。

ex.en: Some politicians are pure [[opportunists]].
ex.zh: 有些政客完全是投机分子。

vocab.note: leave sth lying around = 把东西乱放。也可以说人“闲躺着”：lie around all day。

ex.en: Don't leave your keys [[lying around]].
ex.zh: 别把钥匙到处乱放。

ex.en: There were toys [[lying around]] everywhere.
ex.zh: 到处都乱扔着玩具。

vocab.note: in decline = declining。也说 go into decline（开始衰落）、a decline in sth（……的下降）。

ex.en: The old industry has been [[in decline]] for years.
ex.zh: 那个老行业已经衰落多年了。

ex.en: Bee numbers are [[in decline]] in many countries.
ex.zh: 许多国家的蜜蜂数量在减少。

vocab.note: even as 引出同时发生、方向相反的事：Prices rose even as wages fell.（工资下降的同时物价却在上涨。）

ex.en: The town grew quieter [[even as]] the city boomed.
ex.zh: 城市繁荣起来的同时，小镇却越来越冷清。

ex.en: He kept smiling [[even as]] he lost the game.
ex.zh: 就在输掉比赛的时候，他还一直在笑。

vocab.note: thrive 指在某种环境下长得好、过得好：Plants thrive in sunlight. thrive on sth = 靠……茁壮成长。形容词 thriving。

ex.en: Tomatoes [[thrive]] in warm weather.
ex.zh: 番茄在暖和的天气里长得好。

ex.en: Some people [[thrive]] under pressure.
ex.zh: 有些人越有压力越出色。

vocab.zh: 很难说得过去、很难找到理由
vocab.note: justify：证明……有道理、为……辩护。名词 justification。The end justifies the means. = 为达目的不择手段。

ex.en: Such a high price is [[hard to justify]].
ex.zh: 这么高的价格很难说得过去。

ex.en: How can you [[justify]] spending so much?
ex.zh: 你怎么解释花这么多钱是合理的？

vocab.note: 常用来引出最后的办法，带点幽默：When all else fails, read the instructions.（实在不行，就看说明书吧。）

ex.en: [[When all else fails]], turn it off and on again.
ex.zh: 实在不行，就关了再开一次。

ex.en: [[If all else fails]], we can take a taxi.
ex.zh: 要是其他办法都不行，我们就打车。

m: look the bird in the eye
vocab.note: 表示坦然或敢于面对：He couldn't look me in the eye.（他不敢正眼看我，常暗示心虚。）

ex.en: He couldn't [[look me in the eye]].
ex.zh: 他不敢正眼看我。

ex.en: She [[looked him in the eye]] and said no.
ex.zh: 她直视着他的眼睛说了不。

cloze.hint: 直视（___ sb in the eye）

breakdown.en: Many species are in decline at sea even as their urban cousins thrive, which makes culling them hard to justify.
points: 主句是 Many species are in decline at sea：许多种类在海上数量在减少。
even as their urban cousins thrive 是状语从句，even as 表示“与此同时却……”，把海上和城里两种情况对比起来。
which 引导非限制性定语从句，指代前面整句话的情况，不是指某个名词。
makes culling them hard to justify：make + 宾语 + 形容词。宾语是动名词短语 culling them，补语是 hard to justify。
整句的逻辑：海鸥在海上本来就在变少，所以就算在城里很烦人，也不好随便捕杀。
